title: EurFMT Registry – European Academic Fecal Microbiota Transfer Registry
summary:
Every person is colonized by various microorganisms, such as bacteria, viruses, and fungi (the human microbiome), which vary depending on the site of colonization (e.g., skin, gastrointestinal tract, lungs). Repeated use of antibiotics can lead to a shift or disruption in the composition of the gut microbiota. As a result, infections with the bacterium Clostridioides difficile, for example, as well as other diseases, may occur.
One way to treat diseases associated with a change in the composition of the microbiota is fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). This involves the transfer of filtered components of stool from a healthy donor to an affected recipient.
In this study, we aim to gain a better understanding of FMT and its use by creating a Europe-wide registry containing FMT treatment and safety data from various countries. This registry is intended to provide a comprehensive overview of how FMT is performed in Europe and thereby promote the development and adoption of this microbiota-based treatment in clinical practice.
For this reason, data on the clinical course of the disease and treatment, as well as relevant health data and other measures related to the participants FMT therapy, will be documented in the registry. 
Data collection can be conducted either retrospectively in an anonymized form or prospectively in a pseudonymized form.

Inclusion criteria:

Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient with any social or logistical condition which in the opinion of the investigator may interfere with the conduct of the study, such as incapacity to well understand, not willing to collaborate, or cannot easily be contacted after discharge (only applicable for patients providing prospective pseudonomized data).

It is encouraged that patients included in other clinical trials are also included in the registry, as long as there is no conflict with the inclusion or exclusion criteria of the EurFMT Registry and the other protocol is not in conflict with the means of data collection and publication of this protocol.
